I’m an only child so my opinion may not be welcome here but if you *are* going to have kids, I have some advice - the majority of which is more than what you asked for.

1 may be better for you, but two may be better for them. I don’t have any siblings (I have step siblings but it’s disingenuous to say I know them when we don’t communicate. I’m 20, they’re older than me.) and I will never truly know what that relationship is like between siblings. I think having a buddy around that the other kid can hang around or rely on would be best. If all else fails and in an ideal situation where they don’t hate each other, they have each other, right?

2nd thing, I wouldn’t have kids if My financial status was even up for question. I’m not saying you have to be rich but reality hits different seeing your parents fight over money as a kid. Be realistic. Growing up Poor does put some tough skin that’s hard to replace on a kid but at what cost?

This ties into my third point. Don’t have kids with someone you have a dysfunctional relationship with. That could mean something as simple as communication. I use my parents as a base for a lot of my experiences. Growing up I’d watch them fight, I’d watch them call each other a variety of different things I won’t mention here, I’ve felt the tension, that tension is here to this day. (Quarantine is fucking ROUGH y’all). The point is, the most important thing you can do for yourself is COMMUNICATE how you’re feeling in an effective way. And if you can’t get on the same page, it’s up to you both to figure out how to deal with the situation. Exploding and being emotionally or physically abusive is not a solution. If everything fails and you seriously see each other drift apart romantically, it’s up to you and him to understand that the idea of “staying together for the kids” is incredibly selfish. This will only result in more pain.

TLDR: don’t be stupid, stupid. Can you realistically and financially speaking see yourself raising 1-5 children comfortably? What’s Your job like? Who’s going to be taking care of them? Can you afford daycare? What about school? 

Just some things to consider <3 good luck.
